claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis (also called Epiphanius of Constantia) was bishop of Salamis (Constantia) on Cyprus and lived circa 310–403.
He authored a Greek homily entitled “Homilia in festo palmarum” (Homily for Palm Sunday).
The homily was composed for the celebration of Palm Sunday, the movable feast that commemorates Christ’s triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
In the opening of the sermon Epiphanius addresses the gathered Christian congregation, exclaiming “Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιὼν…” and urging all the Church to rejoice.
The text survives in Greek manuscript tradition and is printed in Migne’s Patrologia Graeca (vol. 41‑43) as well as in modern digital editions such as Documenta Catholica Omnia.
